title: Maharashtra Scraps State Bus Fare Hike for Diwali; Private Operators Cap Theirs
excerpt: MSRTC dropped its planned 15% festive hike outright, citing drought-hit households; private operators plan to hold their increases to 25–30%, below the 50% ceiling.
body:
• Maharashtra's state transport corporation MSRTC has dropped its planned 15% Diwali fare hike, which would have applied from November 1 to 15; standard fares will apply.
  • Transport Minister Pratap Sarnaik confirmed the decision on October 15, citing households already hit by inflation and drought.
  • Private operators, who may legally charge up to 50% above the comparable state fare, plan to limit Diwali hikes to 25–30%, the Pune District Luxury Bus Owners Association said.
  • Passengers remain sceptical: Pune–Bengaluru fares have more than doubled in past festival seasons, and enforcement by the RTO will decide what the cap is worth.

Maharashtra's state bus fares will not rise for Diwali after all. The Maharashtra State Road Transport Corporation has dropped its planned 15% festive hike — which would have run from November 1 to 15 — and Transport Minister and MSRTC chairperson Pratap Sarnaik confirmed on Thursday that standard fares will apply instead, Mirror Now reported. The rationale was the same one travellers would have given: households are already carrying inflation, and farmers are dealing with drought; the corporation would absorb the operational hit rather than pass it on.

The state has declared drought in 305 talukas this year, which frames the politics of the decision. MSRTC fares had already risen 13.56% in July 2026, and a proposed 30% Ganeshotsav surcharge was also withdrawn after opposition, particularly from Konkan commuters, Nation Press reported.

Private Operators Cap, Not Freeze

Private buses are a different market. State guidelines allow private operators to charge up to 50% more than the base fare of a comparable MSRTC service. Balasaheb Khedekar, president of the Pune District Luxury Bus Owners Association, said operators plan to limit Diwali hikes to 25–30% — well under the ceiling, but not a freeze, according to Mirror Now. He pointed to high fuel costs, the absence of government subsidies that MSRTC receives, and long-distance buses returning from outside Maharashtra with low occupancy.

Not everyone in the industry thinks a voluntary cap is enough. Ravindra More of Prasanna Purple Mobility Solutions called for the transport department and RTOs to act more firmly against operators charging exorbitant peak prices.

What Travellers Should Expect

On state buses: no Diwali surcharge. On private buses: budget for a hike of up to about 25–30% if the association's plan holds — and treat quotes far above that as exactly the overcharging the industry itself is arguing about. Passengers told Mirror Now that Pune–Bengaluru fares have more than doubled in previous festival seasons, with overcrowding and extra en-route pickups common; the cap's real test is RTO monitoring during the rush, not the announcement before it.
